title: A sequence-conditioned generative model yields SARS-CoV-2 Mpro and spike inhibitors
summary: A target sequence-conditioned deep generative model sampled drug-like molecules against SARS-CoV-2 Mpro and the spike receptor binding domain. Two of four synthesized candidates per target showed micromolar inhibition in vitro. The most potent spike RBD inhibitor was a rare non-covalent antiviral with activity against several variants in live virus neutralization assays. Potency is micromolar only, and this 2022 preprint was reviewed from the abstract.
ai_technology: Target sequence-conditioned deep generative model for molecule design
organization: IBM Research - Thomas J. Watson Research Center

evidence.tested: In vitro enzymatic and binding assays and live virus neutralization assays.
evidence.unknown: Optimization beyond micromolar potency and any in vivo activity; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: The generative model proposed the inhibitor molecules that were synthesized.
